function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here are a few ways you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty item, or a nationwide delivery: | Option | What it offers | How to get started | |--------|----------------|--------------------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for supporting small businesses | • Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp.
• Call or visit the bakery’s website to place an order.
• Many local shops now accept online orders via their own site or through platforms like **DoorDash** or **Uber Eats**. | | **Specialty cake delivery sites** | Gourmet, artisanal, or themed cakes shipped nationwide | • **Goldbelly** – delivers from renowned bakeries across the U.S. (e.g., Magnolia Bakery, Baked by Melissa).
• **BakeShop** – offers a curated selection of high‑end cakes and pastries. | | **Online marketplaces** | Wide variety of styles, price points, and customization options | • **Etsy** – find independent bakers who ship to your area.
• **Amazon Handmade** – some sellers offer custom cakes (check shipping policies). | | **Big‑box grocery delivery** | Convenient, often same‑day delivery | • **Instacart** – many local bakeries partner with Instacart for quick delivery.
• **Shipt** – similar service in select regions. | | **Social media & community groups** | Local recommendations, often free or low‑cost | • Join local Facebook groups or Nextdoor communities and ask for cake recommendations.
• Instagram hashtags like #YourCityBakery or #CakeDelivery can lead you to hidden gems. | ### Quick Tips for Ordering a Cake 1. **Check delivery times** – especially if you need the cake for a specific event. 2. **Read reviews** – look at recent ratings on Google, Yelp, or the bakery’s own site. 3. **Ask about customization** – most bakeries can accommodate dietary restrictions (gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free). 4. **Confirm the pickup or delivery address** – some sites require a ZIP code to verify availability. 5. **Place your order early** – for holidays or special occasions, bakeries can book up weeks in advance. If you let me know your city or ZIP code, I can pull up a list of highly rated local bakeries and their contact details. Happy cake hunting!
